objective: Implement ReportWorkerPool (start/stop/submit/run_job) executing jobs through the C3 state machine with retry/backoff (1s/4s/16s, max 3 attempts), unit-tested against an in-memory fake of the frozen JobStore interface C5

concepts: in-memory test fake for interface contract C5

frozen_contracts.spec: States queued, running, retry_wait, done, failed. Legal transitions: queued->running; running->retry_wait (attempt < 3, backoff 1s/4s/16s by attempt number); running->done; running->failed (attempt == 3); retry_wait->running; retry_wait->failed (attempt == 3). Crash recovery: any row with status running at startup transitions running->queued (recompute, idempotent per A-2); rows in retry_wait resume their schedule. attempts increments when leaving running toward retry_wait or failed; progress written by the worker between 0..100.

ReportWorkerPool (app/services/report_worker.py): start(session_factory), stop(), submit(job_id: str) -> None (no-op if already queued in pool); run_job(job_id) executes one job to terminal state honoring C3. Pool size fixed at 3. Callable synchronously from tests.

JobStore (app/services/job_store.py), methods on a session: create_job(input_payload: dict) -> ReportJob (status queued); get(job_id) -> ReportJob|None; transition(job_id, from_status, to_status, **fields) -> ReportJob, raises IllegalTransition on illegal C3 transition; recover_stale(now) -> list[ReportJob] (running rows, per C3 recovery).

non_goals: Do not touch app/db/**, app/api/**, or app/main.py
Do not implement or modify JobStore (consume the C5 interface via a test fake)
Do not add a scheduler library — backoff sleep is stdlib
Do not add metrics/logging infrastructure beyond the existing repo pattern
implementation_constraints: All state changes go through JobStore.transition (never direct model writes) so C3 legality is enforced in one place
run_job must be callable synchronously in tests (C4); the pool uses stdlib threading with 3 workers
attempts increments when leaving running toward retry_wait or failed (C3)

deliverables.what: unit test suite (incl. in-memory C5 fake)

acceptance_tests.description: submit enqueues a job; run_job transitions queued -> running, calls generate_report once, and writes status 'done' with progress 100 and result_ref set
acceptance_tests.evidence: pytest tests/services/test_report_worker.py::test_run_to_done asserts row.status == 'done', row.progress == 100, result_ref not null

acceptance_tests.description: generator raises on attempts 1 and 2 (row writes status 'retry_wait', attempts 1/2) and on the 3rd raise writes status 'failed' with attempts 3 and error set; generate_report is called exactly 3 times
submit for a job id the pool already holds is a no-op — a test asserts the pool queue count stays 1
acceptance_tests.evidence: pytest tests/services/test_report_worker.py::test_submit_idempotent asserts queue length == 1 after double submit

acceptance_tests.description: stop() drains the pool: after stop returns, worker threads are joined (active thread count 0)

failure_cases.expected_behavior: error recorded on the row as {code: 'generation_failed', message: str(exc)} per C6; the attempt counts against the 3-attempt budget

failure_cases.scenario: JobStore.transition raises IllegalTransition (should be impossible under C3 usage)
failure_cases.expected_behavior: run_job re-raises; the pool does not swallow the exception — surfacing contract misuse is the intended behavior

handoff.notes: Record the exact backoff schedule implementation and the attempts-increment point in verified_facts — T05 will diff them against C3

warnings.detail: p80 upper bound (120 min) exceeds the Stage budget leaf_p80_max (90 min)
warnings.rationale: concurrent pool plus retry/backoff logic is the densest logic in the Stage; if execution exceeds p80, checkpoint_and_split around the retry-policy boundary
